name: 01-editorial-atlas
prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create one exceptionally polished high-fidelity desktop web application UI reference image, landscape 1536x1024 composition, straight-on full-bleed interface, no laptop/device mockup, no perspective, no surrounding presentation board. Product is the existing "Day, together" multi-agent travel day planner, redesigned as a trustworthy itinerary workspace that can repair a disrupted day while preserving user-locked stops. This is an aspirational product design reference. Render readable restrained typography, purposeful hierarchy, crisp realistic UI spacing, thin line icons, coherent alignment, genuinely useful screen contents. Avoid generic startup landing pages, giant marketing headings, giant empty hero sections, random charts, neon gradients, unreadable tiny text, repeated cards with no meaning. Show a single complete workspace screen for "Tokyo / Your day". Key interface vocabulary: "Plan", "Explore", "Changes", "$100 budget", "$82 estimated", "Demo scenario", "Rain at 14:00", "2 stops changed", "17:00 Tea ceremony" with lock icon, "Repair my day". Include an illustrated city street map with connected numbered route pins, an itinerary timeline, an unobtrusive four-agent collaboration indicator (Planner, Transport, Dining, Activities) as secondary UI, and a clear compact old versus revised schedule comparison explaining the two changed stops. Source and feasibility indicators must be framed as sample interface labels within a "Demo scenario", not actual verification claims. Keep text short and natural; a design reference, not a data-heavy screenshot. EDITORIAL ATLAS. Sophisticated light editorial travel tool. Warm ivory #f6f3eb background, dark forest green ink, muted terracotta accents, fine tan dividers. Confident literary serif headings paired with highly readable geometric sans-serif UI labels. Narrow left navigation, middle itinerary column with generous rhythm and small tactile image thumbnails, broad right cartographic map in pale sage and cream occupying 48% screen. Main header 'A little rain. Still a lovely day.' in elegant moderate-size serif, not enormous. Small rain alert with terracotta repair button. In the itinerary a beautifully composed before/after inset for an outdoor walk replaced by a gallery visit, with locks preserved. Quiet luxury, modern cartographic magazine, feels crafted for people who love travel; no over-rounded dashboard tile overload.

name: 06-spacious-agent-workspace
prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Generate a single exquisite high-fidelity desktop web app UI reference, landscape 1536x1024, crisp full-bleed straight-on screenshot, no device, no perspective. Redesign "Day, together", an educational multi-agent travel planner, specifically around showing actual agent work and communication with abundant whitespace. USER PRIORITY: EXTREMELY UNCLUTTERED, SPACIOUS, EASY TO UNDERSTAND. No route map, no photos, no weather dashboards, no marketing hero, no left sidebar, no visible full itinerary. This is a focused live collaboration workspace. Warm off-white #f7f8fa canvas, white surfaces, midnight navy text, restrained cobalt blue accent, very subtle slate borders, modest green and amber state chips, clean elegant large sans-serif typography. Only TWO main content regions. Top horizontal bar: small 'Day, together' brand left, two simple tabs 'Agent workspace' active and 'Itinerary' inactive. Below one compact inline input row 'Tokyo' 'History, food' '$100' and a cobalt 'Plan my day' button. Main region fills remaining screen: LEFT 65% broad open white canvas labeled 'Live collaboration', RIGHT 35% a clean message inspector labeled 'Communication'. Four well separated substantial rectangular agent cards laid out as a hub and spokes with straight purposeful connector paths: 'Planner' centered above, 'Transport' lower-left, 'Dining' lower-center, 'Activities' lower-right. Important architecture accuracy: ONLY Planner to Transport, Planner to Dining, Planner to Activities connections, bidirectional with clearly directional small moving message dots. NO direct specialist-to-specialist connections. All four agent cards contain just role name, a quiet status chip, and one concrete short current action. Planner: 'Working · Assembling itinerary'; Transport: 'Done · $18'; Dining: 'Done · $32'; Activities: 'Done · $46'. Amber single selected Activities-to-Planner connector with label 'Revised response'. Small neutral canvas caption 'Communication routed by the orchestrator'. Show a restrained tiny legend 'Working  /  Done  /  Revising' in canvas corner. RIGHT message inspector displays only three spacious actual message events with sender, recipient, timestamp, message type chip, and human-readable body: 'Planner → Activities' 'Revision request' 'The plan is $12 over budget. Find an option under $50.'; 'Activities → Planner' 'Revised response' 'Replaced the paid exhibit with a free gallery walk. New total: $46.'; 'Planner → Team' 'Review' 'Updated estimate: $96 of $100.' This last Team entry is a concise summary, not a specialist-to-specialist connection. Each message row has discrete 'Details' disclosure, NO JSON dump shown by default. At inspector bottom a subtle selectable event row 'Selected event · Revised response'. At page bottom one quiet status bar '3 specialists dispatched in parallel' and small 'View itinerary →' link, no performance graphs or stat cards. Clearly legible text, 32px gutters, generous 24px card padding, calm flat design, no excessive nesting, no tiny dense details, no gradients, no glassmorphism, no glowing sci-fi, no robot emoji. Explainability comes from actual messages and current actions, NOT fictional internal chain-of-thought. Design must feel beautiful through spacing, typography, and hierarchy. This is the spacious agent communication alternative to crowded travel dashboards.
